newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM to launch Asia conference on reforms.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM to launch Asia conference on reforms.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda will inaugurate on Thursday an international conference to review economic reforms in India and other major Asian economies, delegates to the conference said on Wednesday.
They said the conference with the theme of "Moving to the market: sustaining reforms in India and Asia", will host delegates from 17 countries.
The conference is being organised by a U.S.-based Asia society in partnership with the Confederation of Indian Industries (CII) and Dow Jones.
"There will be examinations of macroeconomic trends in Asia and geopolitical developments and how they affect the rest of the world," said Susan Heinz of Asia Society.

"Roundtable sessions at the conference will focus on the prospect for infrastructure development, privatisation of public sector industries, financial sector liberalisation and reform of labour and land laws in Asia," Heinz said.
She said the conference assumed added significance as it was being organised just one week after Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram presented the budget for 1997/98 (April-March).

Chidambaram's budget has been welcomed by industry, stock markets and foreign institutional investors. Carla Hills, a former U.S. trade representative and chairman of the Hills and Company will address the meeting on Friday followed by World Trade Organisation's deputy director Chulsu Kim, Thailand's commerce minister Narongchai Aakrasanee and Indian Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah and Chidambaram.

Other keynote speakers from Asia would be Vietnamese Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet, Indonesia's Production and Distribution Coordination Minister Hatarto Sastrosoenarto and Singapore's Information and Arts Minister George Yeo.
